questions.q: Which five things does configuring a REST step involve?
options: HTTP method, endpoint URL, headers, request body, and response mapping
Only a method and an endpoint URL, nothing else
A trigger condition, a condition builder, and an approval step
A spoke name, a channel, and a message
questions.explain: A REST step is configured with a method, endpoint, headers, body, and how the response maps back into data pills.

questions.q: Why does a well-built REST step typically reference a Connection & Credential Alias instead of a hardcoded URL and credential?
options: Aliases are required by ServiceNow and cannot be avoided under any circumstances
Hardcoding is actually the recommended approach for REST steps
The alias stores the connection details once, centrally and securely, so rotating a credential in one place updates every flow that references it
Aliases eliminate the need for authentication entirely
questions.explain: The Connection & Credential Alias is ServiceNow's reusable mechanism for storing connection details once instead of duplicating them per flow.

questions.q: How is a REST step's request body typically populated?
options: It must always be left empty
Using data pills carried forward from the trigger or earlier actions in the flow
By manually typing a new value every time the flow runs
Only by referencing another flow's output, never the current flow's own data
questions.explain: The request body is usually built from data pills carried forward from earlier in the flow, like an incident number or short description.

questions.q: What happens to a field extracted from a REST step's JSON response?
options: Nothing — response data cannot be used elsewhere in the flow
It automatically deletes the triggering record
It's mapped into a new data pill that later steps in the flow can reference, just like any other action's output
It replaces the REST step's own configuration
questions.explain: Response mapping turns a field from the JSON response into a data pill usable by subsequent flow steps.

questions.q: Where does the REST step sit relative to a Script step and a spoke action?
options: It replaces spokes entirely and should always be used instead of one
It's more structured than a Script step (no code) and more general than a spoke (not limited to systems with a pre-built action set)
It is identical to a Script step in every respect
It can only be used for systems that already have a spoke
questions.explain: Reach for a spoke when one exists; reach for the REST step, which needs no code and isn't limited to spoke-covered systems, when it doesn't.
